title: [performance] judging counts only the tasks the gate can still land: a review mission's reported or accepted task (accepted is final) no longer holds deploy-on-landing's quiet spell for ever, so 160's fast path fires
prompt:
Spawn, objective 168 [performance] (projects-47, 2026-11-14: 160's follow-up, scoped by rev-f, confirmed by the lead with N3 dropped; reviewer rev-e): `judging` counts only the tasks the gate can still land, so 160's fast path can fire. (R2: rev-e's F1, the gated mission that accepts by review.)

Line: core line 5 [performance], north star report_to_live.

Why. 160 made deploy/on-landing.sh keep its 5-minute quiet spell only while `spawn mission landing`'s `judging` > 0: the source's tasks in state reported, accepted or landing, each of which may land within a gate's time. But only a gated mission's task is landed by the integrator: a gate-accepted task is `landing` (schema.sql: `when 'accepted' then 'landing'`), and only integrate/landing.rs records task.landed. A review (ungated) mission's reported task waits for a person, and its task.reviewed `accepted` is final: spawn_task_may_continue keeps `accepted and not gated` for good, even after the mission closes. So such a task holds `judging` above 0 for ever, and every landing pays the whole quiet spell, as before 160.
- On live (the lead's read-only SELECTs, 11-14): ungated missions 7 and 8 (owner work, active) hold 40 and 14 tasks in `accepted`, and ungated missions 1 to 3 (done) 7 more. Missions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 all have `sources ->> 0` = spawn.git (8 is supply-pa, 9 flake-doctor).
- So Spawn's `judging` today is 49 under 160's count and 2 with `m.gate is not null`. 160's fast path has never fired for Spawn; 168 makes it reachable.
- Likewise, a gated mission that accepts by review (`accept = 'review'`) sends a task to its gate only once a person accepted it (task_review refuses a human review where the gate accepts; a stale verdict returns such a task to `accepted`, schema.sql's task.gated fold). Its `reported` task waits for a person and cannot land within a gate's time (rev-e F1).
- 160's review N3 (`and m.state <> 'dropped'`) is dropped: mission.closed already cancels every task the closure rule does not let continue, so a dropped gated mission keeps no reported, accepted or landing task, and the clause could fail no test. N1 (the unit test's "accepted" step is a landing task) is the finding above. N2 (the missing-judging fallback, tested) is in the owner part.

What changes:
(1) crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs MAIN_LANDING's `judging` counts only the gate's inputs and what is past them: `and m.gate is not null and (t.state <> 'reported' or m.accept = 'gate')`, in the same states (reported, accepted, landing). The doc comments on MAIN_LANDING and `main_landing` say so and why.
(2) crates/spawn-postgres/tests/deploy.rs `judging_counts_the_sources_tasks_between_report_and_landing` (same name): the gate-accepted step is named for what it is ("a gate-accepted task (landing)"); a mission without a gate on the source with a reported task, then that task reviewed and accepted, leaves `judging` at 2 both times; a gated mission that accepts by review leaves it at 2 with its task reported and makes it 3 once a person accepted it; after the landing, 2.
Owner part (168-owner.diff, deploy/, protected):
(3) deploy/test-on-landing.sh: its mission is configured gated (`spawn mission configure --accept gate --gate <scratch dir>`), as the live Spawn mission is, so its judged cases still count under (1); it accepts by its gate, so its reported task stays counted, and its comment says so (rev-e n1). A new case, "an answer without judging": with nothing judged, a wrapper binary that drops `.judging` from `mission landing` keeps the quiet spell and reads as one judged; with the real binary again, main deploys at once (160's fallback, tested: rev-e's N2).
(4) deploy/on-landing.sh: its header's debounce item says "the source's gated missions" and why. Comment only.
The owner part can land before or with the fleet part: the new test-on-landing passes with the base binary too (its mission is gated). The old test with the new binary fails, because its mission is ungated; deploy.sh switches the script and the binary together.

Never changed: the three states, the quiet and max-wait variables and every other wait of on-landing.sh, what is deployed, the schema.

Cost: `judging` is read every deploy-on-landing tick (a minute). One more filter on the same join; no new index. The lead's EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the gated count on live (11-14, R1's form): 0.62 ms planning, 0.49 ms execution; R2 adds one condition on the same rows. The read, for reference (Spawn's source path in place of $1):
  select count(*) from mission_tasks t join mission_missions m on m.id = t.mission_id where t.state in ('reported','accepted','landing') and m.gate is not null and (t.state <> 'reported' or m.accept = 'gate') and m.sources ->> 0 = $1;
Which missions share Spawn's source was read by the lead with:
  select id, gate is not null as gated, state, sources ->> 0 from mission_missions where id in (1,2,3,7,8);
and, for R2, the kind of each Spawn-source gated mission and the state of each counted task (rev-e):
  select m.id, m.accept, t.state, count(*) from mission_tasks t join mission_missions m on m.id = t.mission_id where t.state in ('reported','accepted','landing') and m.gate is not null and m.sources ->> 0 = $1 group by 1,2,3 order by 1;

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/tests/deploy.rs (168-fleet.diff); deploy/test-on-landing.sh, deploy/on-landing.sh (168-owner.diff); rsi/scenarios/168.sh (the owner's, the contract). One crate. No other open objective touches them.
Size: missions.rs +13 -4, deploy.rs +59 -6; test-on-landing.sh +29 -3, on-landing.sh +4 -3; 168.sh 235.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/168.sh, black box through `spawn mission landing --source S` on a store seeded as 052 and 066 do, with S a bare git repository with a main: gated mission 1's task 1 reported and task 2 gate-accepted (landing); review mission 2's task 3 reported and task 4 reviewed and accepted; gated mission 3 on another source, task 5 reported; gated mission 4 on S accepts by review, its task 6 reported and task 7 accepted by a person. The folded states are checked first (a harness check).
(1) judging is 3 (tasks 1, 2 and 7).
(2) once task 2 has landed, judging is 2.
On the base (80debd0f) 168.sh exits 1: "(1) … expected [3], got [6]", "(2) … expected [2], got [5]". With R1's rule (the gate clause alone) it exits 1 too: "got [4]", "got [3]".

Tests: the unit test above; test-on-landing.sh (owner). Each rule removed alone fails a test or the scenario: without either clause (the base), the unit test (3 for 2) and 168.sh (1) (2) fail; without the accept clause (R1), the unit test ("a gated mission's reported task waits for a person when it accepts by review": 3 for 2) and 168.sh (1) (2) fail; with the fallback read as 0 in on-landing.sh, test-on-landing's new case fails. No test is renamed or dropped.

Proof (rev-f, sync/obj-168/168-proof.txt).

Verified by (projects-47, after it lands and deploys): `spawn mission landing --source <live>/missions/spawn.git | jq .judging` reads only gated tasks (0 while none is reported or landing). Then the report_to_live median over the next day against the day before: 160's fast path fires, so mission 4's landed-to-live slice falls by up to the 5-minute quiet, and the fleet median by about 2 min (160's counterfactual C).
